findings: Separate child interpreter/executable execution and removal of parent-shell eval fallback are already approved by C-D54/SPEC; no new user decision is required.
Fail-closed handling for incompatible hook/trap or unverifiable job state is already approved, while intentional same-user helper/event forgery remains outside the security boundary.
Retaining Bash-first and the selected actual sh/dash fallback is consistent with existing approval; dropping dash would not remove the core ownership races.

The proposed Ctrl-Z-to-pause/takeover change should not be approved on the current evidence. The live probe TSTP handler records SIGNAL_TSTP but does not actually stop, while four start/return cells expect a T process state.
The two parent-WAIT TSTP unknowns also need signal disposition and process-group/session discrimination before assigning a cause.
Existing pause/takeover leaves the current host experiment running, so describing Ctrl-Z remapping as suspend or prompt recovery would conflict with C-D49/C-D52.
The 11 broad-suite failures should be preserved and split into removed-path negative controls and equivalent new-path regression tests rather than deleted or treated as eleven production defects.
The six native TSTP unknowns must be re-probed after fixing the fixture/expectation mismatch; they cannot be relabeled passed or unsupported yet.
The six delegated-cgroup skips remain environment-limited evidence consistent with cgroup being non-required.
recommended_next_step: Run a narrow corrected TSTP discrimination before asking the user to change Ctrl-Z product semantics; retain the already-approved child-exec, fail-closed hook, and Bash/sh boundaries.
evidence_notes: The 105 tests / 11 failures / 6 skips observation came from Root host stdout and was not saved as a formal check record.
Oracle performed static read-only review and did not independently rerun runtime checks.
